# NoMail

> A keyboard-first, local-first email client for macOS. Mail lives in a local
> SQLite database on the user's Mac; NoMail has no backend and no servers that
> mail passes through. Free, Developer ID signed, notarized, and auto-updating.
> Licensed FSL-1.1-ALv2 (Fair Source) — each release becomes Apache 2.0 two
> years after it ships.

Not to be confused with the several unrelated products that share the name;
this one is the macOS email client published at https://nomailapp.com.

## Product

- Views, not folders: filter, group, and sort mail like a database query, save
  the result as a named view, pin views as sections of a split inbox.
- Compose in Markdown: a block editor with headings, lists, to-dos, quotes,
  code blocks, snippets with variables, signatures, scheduled send, undo-send.
- On-device AI: auto-labels and thread summaries run a bundled local model on
  Apple Silicon. Nothing leaves the machine unless the user opts into an
  external provider with their own API key.
- Providers: Gmail and Google Workspace, Outlook.com and Hotmail, Fastmail and
  other JMAP servers, iCloud, and generic IMAP — side by side, combined inbox.
- Also: instant local full-text search, snooze and follow-up reminders,
  calendar invite cards with RSVP, extracted sign-in codes, RFC 8058
  one-click unsubscribe, ⌘K command menu.
- Requires macOS 12 or later. On Intel Macs everything works except on-device
  AI, which ships as an Apple Silicon binary.
